subject: Network report — {title} — {date}
all_good: ✅ Everything worked normally in this period.
ids_note: Suricata runs in alert-only mode and does not block anything.
i_outages: Gateway outage alarms during the period: {n}.
i_severe_in: High severity Suricata alerts from outside: {n}.
i_outbound: High severity Suricata alerts on connections this network opened: {n}.
out_heading: Alerts on connections this network opened
out_intro: These connections were opened from inside the network, so they are not somebody reaching in. A rule can also match ordinary bulk traffic, such as peer-to-peer downloads: check which device opened them.
i_smart: SMART reports a problem with a disk.
i_backup_old: The last configuration backup is {n} days old.
i_backup_none: No recent configuration backup was recorded.
i_cap80: {p}% of the monthly data cap is used.
i_cap100: The monthly data cap is exceeded ({p}%).
alert_intro: These devices joined the network for the first time:
alert_hint: If you do not recognise a device, change the Wi-Fi password or block it on the firewall.
test_body: The mail settings work. Scheduled reports will go to: {to}
text_fallback: Open this message in a mail client that shows HTML to see the full report.
test_alert_text: This is a test alert from {host}. If it arrived, alerts reach this channel.
gw_back_text: Gateway {name} came back at {time}, after {duration} down.
gw_flap_subject: Gateway {name} keeps going down and up — {title}
gw_flap_text: Gateway {name} changed state {n} times in 15 minutes. No more alerts for it until it holds one state for 15 minutes.
gw_steady_text: Gateway {name} has been up without a change since {time}.
login_text: {n} failed logins from {address} within 10 minutes, the last at {time}. Services: {services}. User names tried: {users}.
login_names: {n} (the first two characters of up to three: {names})
ips_text: “{signature}” (severity {severity}) from {src} to {dst}: {n} in this minute, the first at {time}. Action: {action}.
vpn_down_text: VPN connection {name} has been down since {time}.
vpn_back_text: VPN connection {name} came back at {time}, after {duration} down.
wd_subject: The hardware watchdog restarted the firewall — {title}
wd_text: The firewall was restarted by its hardware watchdog (record of {time}). Reasons the hardware recorded: {reasons}.
c2_subject: A device tried to reach a command-and-control server — {title}
c2_text: {device} (MAC {mac}) tried to connect to {dst}, an address on {list}, at {time}. The firewall blocked it. The device may be infected: check it.
infected_intro: Devices that tried to reach a command-and-control list in the last 7 days. The firewall blocked them; check these devices.
more_subject: {n} more alerts of the same kind — {title}
more_text: More than {max} alerts of the same kind came in this minute: {n} more were not sent. See the history.
vpn_none: No VPN is configured on this firewall.
vpn_traffic_note: Traffic as each service counts it: IPsec its associations, OpenVPN its encrypted link, WireGuard its transfers. WireGuard keeps no start time: a peer counts as connected while its last handshake is under 5 minutes old.
vpn_log_from: Outages are counted from {time}, when this version began recording them.
web_off: Unbound's DNS statistics are off: turn them on in the settings of Reporting: Unbound DNS.
apps_no_ids: Suricata wrote no application records in this period: Intrusion Detection is off, or its HTTP logging and its extended TLS logging are.
ntopng_apps: Applications by traffic since ntopng last started (ntopng)
mail_none: No mail server log on this firewall (os-postfix).
web_slow: Unbound's query database did not answer within 120 s.
apps_partial: Suricata's log was read for {n} s only: the counts above are from its first part.
audit_none: This firewall has no audit log.
audit_note: From the firewall's audit log (System: Log Files: Audit): a record of the period, not a certificate of compliance. Of a user name typed at a failed sign-in, only the first two characters are shown.
only_iface_off: Network {name}: gone, or without an IPv4 address of its own - the devices shown are the Local network's
anon_note: addresses, MAC addresses and device names masked
i_backup_nopass: The weekly backup by mail is on but has no password, so none is sent.
backup_text: The configuration of {host}, encrypted with the backup password set in Network Report. To restore it: System: Configuration: Backups, choose this file, tick that it is encrypted, and enter that password.
